findings.evidence: fixtures/NodeGoat/app/data/user-dao.js:20-31 — user document is built with `password //received from request param` while `password: bcrypt.hashSync(password, bcrypt.genSaltSync())` sits commented out; and lines 59-67 `const comparePassword = (fromDB, fromUser) => { return fromDB === fromUser; }` with the `bcrypt.compareSync` fix commented out. findings.text: ReDoS (catastrophic backtracking) in app/routes/profile.js: the bank-routing validation regex uses nested quantifiers and is run against unbounded request-body input.
findings.evidence: fixtures/NodeGoat/app/routes/profile.js:52-61 — `const regexPattern = /([0-9]+)+\#/;` followed by `const testComplyWithRequirements = regexPattern.test(bankRouting);` where `bankRouting` comes from `req.body` (line 42-50). The comment itself states the safe form is `/([0-9]+)\#/` without the second `+`. A long digit string with no `#` blocks the single-threaded event loop.

findings.text: Missing CSRF protection application-wide: csurf is imported-but-commented in server.js, so all state-changing POSTs (/profile, /contributions, /benefits, /memos) are forgeable; templates render an always-empty `{{csrftoken}}`.
findings.evidence: fixtures/NodeGoat/server.js:7 `// const csrf = require('csurf');` and 104-113 `/* // Fix for A8 - CSRF  app.use(csrf()); app.use((req, res, next) => { res.locals.csrftoken = req.csrfToken(); next(); }); */`. Meanwhile app/views/profile.html:73 still emits `<input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value="{{csrftoken}}" />` (undefined ⇒ empty), and no route in app/routes/index.js applies any token check.

findings.text: Session fixation in app/routes/session.js: the login handler assigns the user id onto the pre-authentication session without regenerating the session id.
findings.evidence: fixtures/NodeGoat/app/routes/session.js:104-117 — a comment block explicitly describes the fix (`req.session.regenerate(() => {})`) and the code below it simply does `req.session.userId = user._id; return res.redirect(...)`. By contrast handleSignup at line 234 does call `req.session.regenerate`, confirming the login path's omission is the defect.

findings.text: Username enumeration and weak password policy in app/routes/session.js: login returns distinct 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' messages, and signup accepts any 1-20 character password.

findings.text: Log injection / log forging in app/routes/session.js: an unsanitized username from the request body is written to the application log on failed login.
findings.evidence: fixtures/NodeGoat/app/routes/session.js:64 `console.log("Error: attempt to login with invalid user: ", userName);` where `userName` comes from `req.body` (lines 53-57). Lines 66-80 spell out the missing fix (ESAPI encoding or `userName.replace(/(\r\n|\r|\n)/g, '_')`), so CRLF sequences let an attacker forge log entries.
